title: RBI Industrial Outlook Survey: Business Assessment and Expectations Indices
description: Quarterly Reserve Bank survey of Indian manufacturing companies. The Business Assessment Index (BAI) summarises firms' assessment of the quarter just ended (production, order books, capacity utilisation, inventories, employment, exports, finances and profit margins), and the Business Expectations Index (BEI) their expectation for the quarter ahead. Each index is a simple average of nine weighted net responses and ranges from 0 to 200; 100 separates expansion from contraction. Points are stamped on the last day of the calendar quarter they refer to, so the latest BEI point (the coming quarter) is dated one quarter after the latest BAI. Complements capacity utilisation (OBICUS) and PMIs for industrial nowcasting.
source: Reserve Bank of India (Industrial Outlook Survey press releases)

qna.question: What do BAI and BEI measure?
qna.answer: The survey asks manufacturers whether production, order books, capacity utilisation, employment, exports, finances and profit margins increased, stayed the same or decreased this quarter (assessment) and are expected to in the next. Net response = percentage reporting optimism minus percentage reporting pessimism.^BAI is built from the assessment answers and BEI from the expectation answers. Both are composites of nine parameters, scaled around 100.

qna.question: How should I read them?
qna.answer: Above 100 is expansion and below 100 is contraction. Expectations typically run well above assessments (firms are structurally optimistic), so compare BEI with its own history and track BAI as the realised sentiment.^Quarter labels follow the fiscal year (Q1 = April-June); this dashboard dates each point at the end of the corresponding calendar quarter.

qna.question: What are the caveats?
qna.answer: The survey is qualitative, covers roughly 1,000-1,300 manufacturing companies, and the Reserve Bank has revised the index methodology from time to time. Values are as published in each press release; later releases can restate recent quarters slightly (the latest published value wins here).^History is limited to what the press releases carry and parse; the series starts with the oldest release successfully parsed.
